name: Snow Report 2025-11-19 06:05:02
report:
Good morning, Beast family,  

Our first full week of skiing and riding at The Beast is in the books, and it's safe to say this is one of the best starts to the season on record. With 11 inches of fresh snow accumulating over the past seven days and around-the-clock efforts from our snowmaking team, we are expanding our terrain rapidly, and there is no sign of that slowing down. Snowmaking is rolling on over the next couple of days, with snowguns firing around Snowdon, mainly on Bunny Buster, Lower Chute and sections of Great Northern. Crews have also made great progress around Snowshed on Snowshed Slope, Highlander and the Learn to Ski & Ride Area, which we're hoping to have open soon.   

Today is looking like another beautiful day to hit the slopes with mostly sunny skies and comfortable winter temps in the mid-20's, and conditions are shaping up nicely. Our grooming team laid more fresh corduroy for you last night on cruisers including Upper Double Dipper, Great Northern and more. For those of you looking for a challenge, Downdraft Headwall and Mouse Trap have been left ungroomed, and are home to some serious bumps. We've even got some terrain open on natural snow, such as on Lower Catwalk and Upper Ridge Run, but please note that areas of thin cover may exist. Overall, conditions are spectacular consisting of machine groomed hardpack and packed powder. It's still early season out there, so be aware of variable conditions, and please note that beginner terrain is not available at this time. 

For terrain park lovers, we've got 8 features on Reason including two T-boxes, three rails and three tubes, which are all perfect for early season park sessions. Check out the Killington Parks Report to scope out what Park Crew has built. 

The K-1 Express Gondola, North Ridge Quad, and Snowdon Six Express will be spinning from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. As always, check the lifts and trails report for the most current info before you roll out. 

What are you waiting for? Get out there and have a day! 

-Evan

name: Snow Report 2025-11-18 05:46:09
report:
Good morning, Beast Fans,

We received a few scattered showers last night, adding up to an inch of fresh snow on the mountain. November has been providing, and we'll take every bit of snow we can get. Tuesday is shaping up to be a beauty, featuring partly sunny skies and temps ranging from the mid-20s up top to around 30 degrees at the base. Get ready for spectacular conditions and views over thousands of frosted treetops. It’s going to be one of those days that reminds you why you love winter in the Green Mountains.  

The K-1 Express Gondola, North Ridge Quad, and Snowdon Six Express will be spinning from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. again, offering access to 22 trails. Our grooming team has been blending in the fresh snow and laying down beautiful corduroy all night on cruisers including Rime, Lower Bunny Buster, and Mouse Run. For those of you looking for a challenge, Downdraft Headwall and Mouse Trap have been left ungroomed, and are home to some serious bumps. We've even got some terrain open on natural snow, such as on Upper Royal Flush and FIS, but please note that areas of thin cover may exist. 

Overall, conditions are spectacular consisting of machine groomed hardpack and packed powder. It's still early season out there, so be aware of variable conditions, and please note that beginner terrain is not available at this time. As always, check the lifts and trails report for the most current info before you roll out.

Snowmaking is rolling on today, with terrain expansion and continued base-building being the main focus points. We're running the snowguns around Snowdon, mainly on Bunny Buster and Lower Chute. Crews are also beginning the march to connect in Snowshed pod for Thanksgiving weekend by firing up Snowshed Slope, Yodeler and Highlander.

For heading in to our second week of operations, I'd say that the skiing and riding is pretty darn good. Get out there and enjoy it! It's going to be a beautiful day. 

-Austin

name: Snow Report 2025-11-17 06:04:15
report:
Good Morning, Killington,

Winter’s putting in work, and so is The Beast. We picked up 3 inches of fresh snow overnight, adding a little extra cushion to the trails and keeping that early-season stoke going strong.

Skiing and riding are on advanced terrain only, with no beginner terrain available just yet. That said, the snowmaking crew has their sights set on Snowshed and lower-mountain terrain this week, with the goal of welcoming first-timers and cruisers back to the slopes by Thanksgiving weekend—weather permitting.

Today, the K-1 Express Gondola, North Ridge Quad, and Snowdon Six Express will be spinning from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., offering access to 20 trails across Killington’s upper-mountain pod. With top-to-bottom laps in play, you no longer need to walk the Peak Walkway to exit skiable terrain.

Groomers were out overnight laying down the corduroy on Upper Bunny Buster, Lower Chute, and possibly more if the team was able to drop snow in key zones. As always, check the lifts and trails report for the most current info before you roll out.

Today’s weather: Mostly cloudy with occasional snow showers, highs in the 20s, and brisk winds making it feel even colder—wind chills in the single digits are expected. Dress warm and layer up; it’s a day for goggles, face coverings, and insulated everything.

Our snowmakers are back at it with a cold window that looks promising through midweek. Expect to see them lighting up Snowshed Slope, Middle Great Northern, Upper Bunny Buster, and more as they work to expand terrain heading into the Thanksgiving holiday.

And for those looking to get a little creative, the early-season park on Reason is still rocking eight features for your jibbing pleasure. Check out @kmtnparks on Instagram or our Facebook page to peep the setup.

We’ll see you out there!

-Josh

name: Snow Report 2025-11-16 20:24:08
report:
Good afternoon, Killington,       

The Beast took a snowy shower today and came out looking sharp! 

Planning a trip to The Beast? Please note that early-season conditions exist, and skiing and snowboarding are on advanced terrain only for the time being. Beginner terrain is not available right now, though, as long as this upcoming cold snap lasts long enough, our plan is to open dedicated beginner terrain for Thanksgiving weekend.    

The K-1 Express Gondola, North Ridge Quad, and Snowdon Six Express are open from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. tomorrow with skiing and riding on 20 different trails. With peak to base skiing and riding now available, walking is no longer required on the Peak Walkway to exit skiable terrain.   

The grooming team will be smoothing things out for us, getting after sections on Upper Bunny Buster and Lower Chute. Depending on how much snow can be put down, more Snowdon trails will also get some passes. Check out the full mix of groomed terrain on our lifts and trails report. 

Snow is on the menu this afternoon with 1 to 2 inches expected and some heavy squalls rolling through as west winds crank up. Another 2 to 4 inches may stack up tonight before things taper off and wind chills dip well below zero. Monday keeps the winter vibe going with cold, gusty conditions and plenty of blowing snow before settling into a chilly, breezy night. 

The snowmakers have a clear shot through Thursday to fire things up and do what they do best. The goal is to maintain and expand open terrain for the holiday period, specifically targeting Snowshed and connecting it to the Snowdon & K-1 area. The primary focus areas include Snowshed Slope, top of Snowdon, Middle Great Northern, and Upper Bunny Buster. 

Our early season park is offering 8 features on Reason to get involved with. Check out @kmtnparks on Instagram or our Facebook page to peep the setup.  

That’s our first weekend done and dusted. We loved seeing you out there! 

-Evan

Good morning, Beast family,    

You asked for it, and we’re rolling it out: top-to-bottom laps to fire up your weekend! Our crew worked hard to make it happen—get out there and savor it.

As you plan your voyage to The Beast, please note that early-season conditions exist, and skiing and snowboarding are on advanced terrain only for the time being. Beginner terrain is not available right now, though, as long as Mother Nature cooperates, our plan is to open dedicated beginner terrain for Thanksgiving weekend.

We are bringing the people what they’ve been asking for. In addition to the North Ridge terrain we've been offering, we’re unleashing groomed terrain on Middle Great Northern down to Middle Chute and Lower Bunny Buster all the way to the base of the K-1 Gondola. Additionally, the Snowdon Six Express started spinning to provide luxurious bubble travel along with access to Killink and Upper Mouse Run, which are also groomed. Expect conditions on groomed terrain to consist of machine-groomed hardpack and some variable early-season conditions. Due to a grooming tractor issue, both of these estimated opening times may be delayed. Our team is working diligently to address the issue. 

A couple of scattered snow showers rolled through last night and today brings a touch of sunshine and a slight warm-up. The system brought light snow before flipping to an icy mix at the end of the day with about an inch of snow/sleet.  

The Beast’s snowmakers made moves again. They switched gear from North Ridge last night to continue firing on Snowdon into this morning on trails including Mouse Run, Mouse Trap, Full House, Bunny Buster, Killink, Great Northern, and Chute. Before top-to-bottom skiing and riding commences, snowmaking will begin go offline. Temps will gradually rise today, and snowmaking likely comes back online tomorrow night or Monday. 

Our early-season park is looking crisp on Reason with eight features to play with. The park crew works diligently to get us this early-season setup, and it shows. 

Have a safe and fun weekend, fam. Hope to see you out on the hill!    

-Evan
